text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- More than 75 percent of businesses involving foreign capital were operating at a loss during the first eight months of this year, according to a report by the authorities in Ho Chi Minh City.
-- The local partners in a $247 million U.S.-Vietnamese tourist resort venture on Danang's China Beach have informed the Ministry of Planning and Investment that the project has disintegrated.
-- Belgium's Deputy Prime Minister, Philippe Maystadt has arrived in Vietnam for talks on trade and commerce.
-- China's Red Cross Association has given $20,000 to help victims of recent flooding in Vietnam.

-- An $80 million industrial zone joint-venture in Haiphong has been established between U.S. insurer American International Group, International Port Engineering and Management of Belgium, the Asian Infrastructure Development Co of Thailand, and a local partner.
-- A draft anti-corruption ordinance has been completed as part of efforts to tackle graft in Vietnam.
-- Hanoi police have issued orders for the arrest of a senior member of the Interior Ministry's Economic Police Department on suspicion of involvement in a drug trafficking case.
-- Vietnam has joined other countries in Southeast Asia in signing an agreement on strengthening anti-drug activities in the Mekong sub-region.
